strings.zh: 你听说过紫苑镇的由来吗？
strings.en: Have you heard how Lavender Town got{NEWLINE}its name?

strings.zh: 紫苑……{NEWLINE}真的是个很凄美的名字呢。
strings.en: Lavender... It really is a beautiful,{NEWLINE}sad name.

strings.zh: 传说很久很久以前,{NEWLINE}紫苑镇还是一个无名的小村,{CLEAR}村里有一位叫「紫苑」的女孩{CLEAR}跟她的丈夫非常恩爱。{SCROLL}后来关东地区被坏人入侵,{NEWLINE}紫苑的丈夫便决定从军远征保卫家园。{SCROLL}自那以后,紫苑每天都站在村口{NEWLINE}盼望丈夫回来。{CLEAR}可是一年、两年过去了,{CLEAR}她的丈夫始终没有回来,{CLEAR}后来战争结束了,{CLEAR}她的丈夫还是没有回来。{SCROLL}不愿意接受丈夫死亡事实的紫苑{NEWLINE}依然每天守在村口等待丈夫,{CLEAR}结果最终变成了一尊石像。{SCROLL}人们被紫苑对丈夫的一片痴情所感动,{NEWLINE}便用她的名字命名这座村庄为「紫苑村」,{CLEAR}也就是现在紫苑镇的前身了。
strings.en: Legend says that long, long ago,{NEWLINE}Lavender Town was just a little village{CLEAR}with no name.{SCROLL}In the village lived a girl named{NEWLINE}Lavender.{SCROLL}She loved her husband dearly.{SCROLL}Then villains invaded the Kanto region,{NEWLINE}and Lavender’s husband went off to war{CLEAR}to defend their home.{SCROLL}From then on, Lavender stood at the{NEWLINE}edge of the village every day, waiting{CLEAR}for her husband to return.{SCROLL}One year passed, then two, and still he{NEWLINE}didn’t come back. The war ended, and{CLEAR}still he didn’t come back.{SCROLL}Lavender refused to accept that he was{NEWLINE}dead. She kept waiting for him at the{CLEAR}edge of the village every day...{SCROLL}...until at last she turned into a stone{NEWLINE}statue.{SCROLL}Moved by Lavender’s devotion to her{NEWLINE}husband, the people named the village{CLEAR}after her: Lavender Village.{SCROLL}That village grew into the Lavender{NEWLINE}Town of today.
strings.notes: 紫苑 (the girl) → Lavender, so the town-name legend works in English (0336 #1, 0473, 0474 #35).

strings.zh: 我最近又听了些{NEWLINE}关于少女紫苑的传说,{CLEAR}你也想听听吗？
strings.en: Lately I’ve heard more stories about{NEWLINE}the girl Lavender.{SCROLL}Want to hear them too?

strings.zh: 据说紫苑的丈夫{NEWLINE}在死后变成了口袋妖怪鬼斯,{CLEAR}从战场回来跟紫苑相见了。{SCROLL}但是紫苑并不认识变成鬼斯的丈夫,{NEWLINE}于是这位丈夫索性就以鬼斯的形态{CLEAR}默默地陪在紫苑身边,{CLEAR}一陪就是几千年……
strings.en: They say that after Lavender’s husband{NEWLINE}died, he became a Gastly and came home{CLEAR}from the battlefield to see her.{SCROLL}But Lavender didn’t recognize her{NEWLINE}husband as a Gastly.{SCROLL}So he simply stayed by her side as a{NEWLINE}Gastly, quietly keeping her company...{CLEAR}for thousands of years.

strings.zh: 听了紫苑和她丈夫的故事{NEWLINE}不禁让我感叹：{CLEAR}世界上最遥远的距离,{CLEAR}不是生与死的距离,{CLEAR}而是我站在你面前,{CLEAR}你却不知道我爱你。
strings.en: Hearing the story of Lavender and her{NEWLINE}husband makes me think...{SCROLL}The farthest distance in the world isn’t{NEWLINE}the one between life and death.{SCROLL}It’s when I stand right in front of you,{NEWLINE}and you don’t know that I love you.
strings.notes: Quotes a well-known Chinese poem (世界上最遥远的距离, often misattributed to Tagore); translated, not song lyrics.

strings.zh: 谢谢你听我说了这么多故事,{NEWLINE}这个送给你吧！
strings.en: Thanks for listening to all my stories.{NEWLINE}Here, this is for you!
